core_obligations: Show that each N_n = RHom_{X_n}(E|_{X_n}, F_n) is perfect over D(A_n) with base change compatible formation, so that the transition maps are isomorphisms (proof lines 8098-8110).
Use the perfectness of derived limits to get Rlim N_n perfect and identify RHom_X(E, K) with Rlim N_n through the commutation of the exact functor with products (proof lines 8112-8123).
Translate statement (1) into statement (2) by duality (proof lines 8123-8125).
proof_roadmap: Perfectness and base change of the finite level Homs (proof lines 8098-8110).
The derived limit and the identification with RHom_X(E, K) (proof lines 8112-8123).
difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-existence with K as in Lemma labelled lemma-compute-what-it-should-be, the lemma asserts for every perfect object E of D(O_X) that M = RGamma(X, K otimes^L E) is perfect over D(A) with a canonical isomorphism RGamma(X_n, F_n otimes^L E|_{X_n}) = M otimes_A^L A_n, and dually that N = RHom_X(E, K) is perfect over D(A) with RHom_{X_n}(E|_{X_n}, F_n) = N otimes_A^L A_n (statement lines 8078-8096). The proof of (2) writes E_n = E|_{X_n} and N_n = RHom_{X_n}(E_n, F_n), recalls that RHom_{X_n}(-, -) is RGamma(X_n, RSheafHom(-,-)) by Cohomology, Section labelled cohomology-section-global-RHom, and uses Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-base-change-RHom-perfect to see that each N_n is perfect over D(A_n) with base change compatible formation (proof lines 8098-8110). Hence the transition maps N_n otimes^L A_{n-1} -> N_{n-1} are isomorphisms, so More on Algebra, Lemma labelled more-algebra-lemma-Rlim-perfect-gives-perfect shows Rlim N_n is perfect and recovers N_n after base change; since the exact functor RHom_X(E, -) commutes with products and hence with derived limits, RHom_X(E, K) = Rlim RHom_X(E, F_n) = Rlim N_n, giving (2) (proof lines 8112-8123). Statement (1) is translated into (2) with Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-dual-perfect-complex (proof lines 8123-8125). Recognising that the system of perfect complexes is Mittag-Leffler enough for its derived limit to be perfect, and identifying the derived limit with the Hom against K, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
